rootCause.summary: The explicit /weather shortcut routes to the weather_query scenario, which depends on the LLM emitting a weather_lookup tool call (direct_output_from_tool short-circuits only AFTER the call). The configured local model (qwen3:30b) sometimes returns no tool call and no final (llm_returned_no_tool_calls_and_no_final), producing OutcomeProviderError. Because weather_query is requires_provenance and the assembler yields empty Sources, the provenance gate rewrites the provider-error into the capture-as-fallback body 'saved as an idea — i'll surface it later.' Geocoding was never the cause (Open-Meteo resolves the ZIP directly).

resolution: Add a deterministic /weather fast-path (facade Step 3.9) that dispatches the weather tool directly for an explicit /weather <location> shortcut, bypassing the LLM loop AND the provenance gate. Extract weather.LookupForecast (shared core of the tool handler) and wire it as a facade seam (WithWeatherLookup). Success renders forecast_line + one SourceExternalProvider; provider failure / empty location render an honest StatusUnavailable/slot_missing line — NEVER the capture-as-fallback acknowledgement. Backward-compatible: the LLM /weather path is untouched when the seam is not wired. Three adversarial unit tests reproduce the pre-fix provider-error and assert the fast-path bypasses it; regression-quality-guard --bugfix PASS.

The reflected user location never reaches the Telegram wire at all — StatusUnavailable routes to renderError, which emits the single-line "<skill>: <cause>" form and drops resp.Body (:175-180, :300-312). SECRETS: grep for api_key|token|secret|password|credential|auth across the whole non-test weather package returns NO output — the provider is key-less by design (open_meteo.go:9-11) and no Authorization header is set on either request.
